label: About the option “{name}”
language.what: The language of all the texts of Heidrun, and of the names of the days: English or French.
language.how: A click on a language changes the texts at once. Heidrun saves the choice and uses it at the next start.
timeFormat.what: The way that Heidrun writes the time of the day: with AM and PM, or with 24 hours.
workingDays.what: The days of the week on which you work with your coding agents.
goatSound.what: A switch for the goat sound: the goat bleats of the sound button of the About window, of the sound button of the splash screen, and of the smiley of the empty tab screen.
goatSound.on: A click on one of these three places plays a goat bleat, and the bleats play in turn. Switching the switch on plays no sound by itself.
goatSound.off: A click on these three places plays nothing, and a bleat that is playing stops at once. The switch is off at the first start of Heidrun.
font.what: The font of the text in the terminals.
font.how: A click on a font changes all the terminals at once. Heidrun saves the choice. The font Inconsolata for Powerline must be installed on this computer: when you choose it, the page shows the command that installs it.
fontSize.what: The size of the text in the whole Heidrun window, and not only in the terminals.
fontSize.how: The button A+ makes the text larger and the button A− makes it smaller, by half a pixel each time. The button Reset goes back to the default size. Heidrun saves the size.
fontSize.keys: Press ⌘+ to make the text larger, ⌘− to make it smaller, and ⌘0 to go back to the default size.
mouseMode.what: What the mouse does when the pointer is in a terminal.
mouseMode.select: Drag the mouse to select text, and press ⌘C to copy it. The wheel and the clicks no longer go to Herdr.
mouseMode.app: The wheel and the clicks go to Herdr and to the agents. Hold ⌥ and drag the mouse to select text.
agent.title: {name}
agent.what: A switch that tells Heidrun that you can use {name}. Switch it on only when you have a valid subscription or a valid access for {name}.
agent.on: When quota monitoring is on, Heidrun shows the quota of {name} in the status bar. Heidrun also offers the skills of {name} in the windows of the skills.
agent.off: Heidrun hides the quota of {name}, and does not offer the skills of {name}.
quotaMonitoring.what: Whether Heidrun collects and shows account quota data for the coding agents switched on in this section.
quotaMonitoring.on: Heidrun shows available quota data in the status bar. For Claude Code, Heidrun adds quota reporting to its status line and keeps your previous status line working.
quotaMonitoring.off: Heidrun hides quota data and removes its quota reporting from Claude Code. Your previous Claude Code status line is restored.
antigravityTracking.what: Connects Antigravity's status line to Heidrun so that Heidrun can show Antigravity's quota in the status bar.
antigravityTracking.on: Heidrun adds quota tracking and keeps the existing Antigravity status line visible. When Antigravity is switched on in the list above, its quota appears in the status bar.
antigravityTracking.off: Heidrun restores the Antigravity status line that was in use before quota tracking.
antigravityTracking.development: Heidrun Development cannot change the shared Antigravity status line. Change this option in installed Heidrun.
newTab.what: The program that starts in the pane of a new tab.
confirmWorkspaceClose.what: A question that Heidrun asks before it closes a workspace.
confirmWorkspaceClose.on: A click on the button that closes a workspace opens a window that asks you to confirm. The workspace closes only after you confirm.
confirmWorkspaceClose.off: A click on the button closes the workspace at once, without a question.
confirmTabClose.what: A question that Heidrun asks before it closes a tab.
confirmTabClose.on: A click on the button that closes a tab asks you to confirm. Heidrun asks only when the workspace has more than one tab.
confirmTabClose.off: A click on the button closes the tab at once, without a question.
confirmPaneClose.what: A question that Heidrun asks before it closes a pane.
confirmPaneClose.on: A click on the button that closes a pane asks you to confirm. The pane closes only after you confirm.
confirmPaneClose.off: A click on the button closes the pane at once, without a question.
confirmSavedSearchDelete.what: A question that Heidrun asks before it deletes a saved search of the Code hosting sidebar section.
confirmSavedSearchDelete.on: The button that deletes a saved search opens a window that asks you to confirm. The saved search is deleted only after you confirm.
confirmSavedSearchDelete.off: The button deletes the saved search at once, without a question.
projectGuards.title: Guards of the project
projectGuards.what: A guard of the project is a rule that you write for this project. Before Heidrun types a command in a terminal, it checks the command against the guards. A guard asks you to confirm the command, or forbids it.
projectGuards.how: The button Add a guard opens a window where you write the name of the guard, its action, and its lines. The buttons on the row of a guard edit it or remove it. Heidrun writes each change at once in the file .heidrun/config.json of the project.
builtInGuards.title: Hardcoded guards
builtInGuards.what: A hardcoded guard comes with Heidrun, and it is the same in all the projects. It asks you to confirm a command that can do harm.
builtInGuards.read: This button shows the guard in a window, to read only. A hardcoded guard cannot be edited, and it cannot be removed.
builtInGuards.switch: This switch turns the guard on or off for this project only. Heidrun writes the choice at once in the list disabled of the file .heidrun/config.json. A guard that is off is dimmed.
notifyBlocked.what: A reminder that Heidrun sends when an agent waits for you for a long time.
notifyBlocked.how: When an agent stays blocked for this time, Heidrun sends one notification for it. The choice “never” sends no reminder. Heidrun sends no notification during the quiet hours.
notifyContext.what: The context of an agent is all that the agent can remember in a chat. When the context is full, the agent works less well.
notifyContext.on: Heidrun sends one notification when the context of an agent goes above 80 %. After a compaction of the context, Heidrun can warn again.
notifyContext.off: Heidrun sends no notification about the context.
notifyQuota.what: The quota of Claude is the amount of work that your subscription allows, for 5 hours and for one week.
notifyQuota.on: Heidrun sends one notification when a quota of Claude goes above 80 %, and one more notification when it goes above 95 %.
notifyQuota.off: Heidrun sends no notification about the quota. The status bar still shows the quota.
notifyEvening.what: A summary of the work that finished during the day.
notifyEvening.how: Write the time as hours and minutes, for example 18:30. At this time, Heidrun sends one notification with the summary. Leave the field empty to turn it off.
quietHours.what: A period of the day in which Heidrun sends no notification.
quietHours.how: Write the start and the end, for example 20:00 and 08:00. The period can go over midnight. Leave the fields empty to turn it off.
showStatusItem.what: The status item is a small icon of Heidrun in the menu bar of macOS, at the top of the screen. Its menu lists the agents.
showStatusItem.on: The icon is in the menu bar. A click on an agent in its menu selects the pane of this agent in Heidrun.
showStatusItem.off: Heidrun puts no icon in the menu bar of macOS.
showWorkspaces.what: A list of the workspaces. A click on a workspace selects it, and a drag moves it.
finishedTtl.what: How long a finished job stays on the screen.
chatsRefresh.what: How often Heidrun reads the files of the chats again, while the Past chats sidebar section is on the screen.
gitFetch.what: How often Heidrun runs the command git fetch by itself, without a click from you. The choice Off never runs it.
dynamicTopics.what: A dynamic topic is a short subject that Heidrun finds for each chat of the Past chats sidebar section.
dynamicTopics.on: Heidrun finds the topics of the chats, shows them as labels on the chats, and shows the dynamic topic bar. The extraction method decides how Heidrun finds the topics.
dynamicTopics.off: Heidrun shows no dynamic topic bar and no label, computes nothing, and makes no call.
rebuildClusters.what: A clustered dynamic topic is the name of a group of raw dynamic topics that have a close meaning. This button makes all the groups again.
rebuildClusters.how: A click empties the translation table, and groups all the raw dynamic topics again, in one call to the coding agent. The button works only when the option Enable clustered dynamic topics is on.
mobileAccess.what: Mobile access lets you follow the agents from a phone. Heidrun opens a tunnel with the program ngrok, and the phone connects to it.
mobileAccess.on: Heidrun opens an ngrok tunnel. The address of the tunnel is the same each time. A QR code shows the address and the pairing key, and the phone scans it.
mobileAccess.off: Heidrun opens no tunnel, and no phone can connect. The tunnel also closes when you quit Heidrun.
mobileTyping.what: The phone always shows the terminals, to read only. This option lets you type in a terminal from the phone.
mobileTyping.on: The phone still asks you before it lets you type, each time you open a terminal. Every command you type passes the guards.
mobileTyping.off: The phone cannot type in a terminal.
voiceInput.what: The voice input lets you hold a button, speak, and release the button. A short click on the button also works: it starts to listen, and a second click stops. Heidrun changes your speech into text with a Whisper model, on this computer, and writes the text in the composition bar. You read the text, edit it, and send it.
voiceInput.on: Heidrun shows the push-to-talk button in the composition bar, after the button Send. Open the composition bar with the button in the header of the focused pane. The microphone opens only while you hold the button, or between two clicks. Level bars show your voice while it listens. macOS asks for the permission the first time. The sound stays in the memory of this computer: Heidrun never saves it and never sends it.
voiceInput.off: Heidrun shows no push-to-talk button, downloads no model, and never opens the microphone.
voiceInputLanguage.how: “Detect the language” lets Whisper find the language of each recording. A fixed language is faster and more exact. A model whose name ends with .en understands only English, and ignores this choice.
voiceInputModel.what: The Whisper model is the file that changes speech into text. A larger model is more exact and slower, and its file is larger.
voiceInputModel.how: Heidrun downloads the file from Hugging Face when you choose a model that is not on this computer, and writes it in the folder models of the Heidrun folder. Only this download uses the network: the speech never leaves this computer.
compositionBarOnAgentStart.what: Choose the initial visibility of the composition bar when a new pane starts directly with a coding agent. The choice is saved across restarts. Existing panes keep their current visibility. You can still show or hide each composition bar with the button in the pane header.
compositionBarOnAgentStart.on: New panes that start directly with a coding agent show the composition bar. Plain terminals keep the composition bar hidden.
compositionBarOnAgentStart.off: New panes that start directly with a coding agent keep the composition bar hidden until you show the composition bar manually. Off is the default.
colorTeam.what: Choose a named set of colours for the complete application.
colorTeam.how: Click a name to apply its colours immediately. The chosen team is saved on this device and remains selected when the application restarts. The team works with the current light or dark appearance. Coding agent status dots keep their existing colours.
